findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, so the RDS volume, its snapshots, and automated backups store all catalogue data in cleartext on the underlying storage. Any compromise of a snapshot or of the storage layer yields the full dataset.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from outside the VPC, and the endpoint is exported as a Terraform output. This turns the database into internet-facing attack surface for credential brute force and exploitation of MySQL vulnerabilities, relying solely on the security group as a control.

The master user is hard-coded to the well-known default 'admin' and the password is supplied from var.password (no sensitive marking, no secrets manager integration), so the credential appears in plan output and state. Combined with the publicly accessible endpoint this materially lowers the bar for credential guessing.

The database endpoint, master username, and the plaintext master password (var.password) are interpolated directly into the instance user_data script. User data is retrievable unauthenticated from the instance metadata service by any local process or via any SSRF in the PHP application, and is also visible to anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute and in Terraform state.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource "*". Any compromise of the web server yields the ability to read or delete every S3 bucket, manipulate all EC2 resources (including launching instances and modifying security groups), and snapshot, modify, or delete any RDS instance in the account. This violates least privilege and provides lateral movement and privilege-escalation paths.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 remains enabled. A server-side request forgery in the PHP application exposed on this host would allow theft of the instance profile credentials, which carry the wildcard s3:*/ec2:*/rds:* policy. Requiring http_tokens = "required" would block the classic SSRF credential theft path.

No root_block_device or ebs_block_device encryption is configured, so the instance volume — which holds /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc containing the database master password — may be stored unencrypted depending on account defaults.

The MySQL 8.0 parameter group sets only character set options and does not set require_secure_transport = 1. The generated PHP client calls mysqli_connect() with no TLS options, so application-to-database traffic — including the master credentials — can traverse the network in cleartext.

The database security group permits all protocols and all ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0. A database host has no legitimate need for unrestricted internet egress, and this removes a control against data exfiltration and command-and-control callbacks following a database compromise.

iam_database_authentication_enabled is not set, so access depends entirely on the static master password that is distributed in cleartext through EC2 user data. There is no short-lived, centrally revocable credential path to the database.
